title: Startup time and bundle size budget for phones
when: The app feels slow to open on mid range phones and the user wants numeric budgets for startup and JavaScript size, plus a way to hold them.
prompt:
Goal: Written budgets for startup on a mid range phone and a script that fails when the shipped JavaScript grows past them.
Steps:
1. Set budgets in budget.json: startup JS at most 150 KB compressed, CSS 30 KB, largest contentful paint under 2.5 s and interaction delay (INP) under 200 ms on a 4x CPU slowdown with a slow 4G profile.
2. Measure in the page with PerformanceObserver for "largest-contentful-paint" and "event" entries; add performance.mark("app-ready") when the first screen is usable.
3. Split code: load screens with dynamic import() on navigation; the first screen gets only what it needs.
4. Defer non critical work (analytics, prefetch) with requestIdleCallback or a setTimeout fallback after first paint.
5. Preload the hero image or font with <link rel="preload"> only when it is on the first screen.
6. check-size.mjs reads each file in dist, gzips it with node:zlib gzipSync and exits with code 1 when a budget is exceeded.
7. Run the check in CI and print a table of file, size and budget.
Quality bar:
- Budgets are numbers, not wishes.
- The first screen works before secondary chunks load.
Pitfalls:
- Measuring only on a fast laptop.
- One large dependency for a tiny feature.
- Long tasks over 50 ms during startup from parsing big JSON.
Verify:
- [ ] budget.json parses.
- [ ] check-size.mjs exits non zero over budget.
- [ ] Screens are loaded with import().
Output: budget.json, check-size.mjs and a perf section in the README.

examples.input: meu app demora 6 segundos pra abrir no celular
examples.output: budget.json (150 KB JS, LCP 2.5 s), import() per screen, check-size.mjs failing CI over budget
